doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: Refusing first trumpet and winning the lead trumpet pay raise
summary: He and his section refused first parts and proposed a union lead premium of 50 percent, backed by Chuck Mangione.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: So I said you know — so then they started calling me and I’d say, “Okay I’ll play fourth trumpet.” They said, “No, no, we want you to play first.” I said, “Well why should I play first? It’s easier to play fourth. Just have the people that you normally get play first.”
Mmm. Why do you think we called you?

No though then I talked to Al and Jeff and Joe and I said, “Tell them the same thing I said.” So what would happen, the first few times you know they wouldn’t hire us. And the contractor would come and say, “If I come back here I’m going to tell everybody that

there’s no trumpets here, I have to bring in trumpets and somebody’s not going to work.” So just think about that. So then they didn’t want to pay. See they didn’t want to pay so Chuck Mangione actually — I made a proposal to the musicians union. I said, “You know if a saxophone player plays and he plays clarinet and saxophone he gets extra money. I said “That’s good, I said, “I think that’s right.” “Play three and sometimes get double scale for that.” So the second tenor player is making double scale and the lead trumpet player, which is a special skill, is making scale. And so is the fourth trumpet player. I said, “I don’t get that.” I said, “I’d rather play fourth.” This was a musicians union meeting. And they went, “What do you propose?” I said, “I propose that the lead trumpet gets 50% over scale or something equivalent like that.” We get paid for flugelhorn but they tell us not to use it. You see what I mean? Because it would make the contract bigger.

And then Chuck Mangione was there, he came and he supported that. And I don’t know what it is now but I’m sure it’s been rescinded, but the lead trumpet got 50% over scale. So when we played together we took that 50% and split it up.
See? And then we could get through any show.
